Concentrated finding round #4 — first-touch grading (triage seat, session `session_01JEhkB6ShK2HHDzozy7Qwgz`): **promoted to `pm:queue`**, with a Clause-② flag for the dispatching seat.

Verified on `origin/main` @ `12841b6`: the optional `options` bag is declared at `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:462-466`; the sole runner call site at `:988-990` passes one argument (adjacent comment cites the #4314 retirement, landed as PR #5209); the dead-in-practice readers are `packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionConfirmDialog.tsx:58` and `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:190`.

Why queue, not decision: the maintainer already ruled the structured-confirm retirement (#4314, 2026-08-17); this vestigial parameter was deferred for a *scheduling* reason (app-shell held by another session), not a product one — completing a standing ruling is dispatchable. #4314's reopen condition survives this removal.

⚠️ **Clause-② note for the claim**: narrowing a published callback type in `@object-ui/core` makes existing two-parameter handler implementations fail to type-check — a breaking change on the compile contract of a published package (no runtime accept/reject change). The claim comment must declare `Clause-②: yes` per the intake gate, the PR needs a breaking-annotation changeset, and the dev should sweep the consumer radius. Dispatch must also re-check session holds on `packages/app-shell` first, per the body. Serial: ActionRunner.ts churned twice this cycle (#5209, #5218), both merged; no open PR. Size suggestion: S–M, opus.

os-dev-report

**Status: `needs_decision` — STOPPED AT ZERO COMMITS.** The measurement the dispatch
ordered contradicts this card's central premise, so the 回翻条款 applies: I report the
fork rather than re-rule it.

## The premise is false: `options` has a live producer

The card states *"The only producer of that argument was the structured `confirm` arm's
forwarding inside ActionRunner's precedence read"* and concludes *"With no producer,
`options` is now always `undefined` at runtime."*

That is true **only inside `ActionRunner`**. It is false for the repo. A second producer
has existed all along, and it bypasses the runner entirely:

`packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:1397`

```
const confirmed = await confirmHandler(
    t('console.objectView.deleteViewConfirm', { name: viewLabel }),
    {
        title: t('console.objectView.deleteViewTitle'),
        confirmText: t('console.objectView.delete'),
        cancelText: t('console.objectView.cancel'),
    },
);
```

That `confirmHandler` is destructured at `ObjectView.tsx:911` from
`useConsoleActionRuntime`, whose `ConsoleActionRuntime.confirmHandler` is declared
`ConfirmationHandler` at `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:78`. So this is the published type
being invoked with a fully-populated, fully-localized options bag.

**It is reachable UI, not dead code**: the enclosing `handleDeleteView`
(`ObjectView.tsx:1389`) is wired at `ObjectView.tsx:2472`
(`onDeleteView={isAdmin ? handleDeleteView : undefined}`) and `:2486`
(`onDelete={handleDeleteView}`) — the admin "delete saved view" confirmation.

`git blame`: the call and its three localized keys date to **2026-08-10** (`5bfaabde0`,
`36ae2705b4`) — they predate both the #4314 ruling (2026-08-17) and the triage
(2026-08-19). Nothing regressed; the search was simply scoped to the runner.

**Consequence**: removing `options` does not delete inert surface. It silently deletes a
working feature — the delete-view dialog would lose its title and both button labels and
fall back to the generic `actionConfirm.*` strings.

## Consumer census (with counter-probes)

| Site | Role | Reads/writes `options` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core/.../ActionRunner.ts:988` | producer (runner) | no — passes 1 arg |
| `app-shell/.../ObjectView.tsx:1397` | **producer** | **writes all 3 fields, localized** |
| `app-shell/.../useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:190` | implementer `(message, options)` | **reads** — forwards to `setConfirmState` `:192` |
| `app-shell/.../RecordDetailView.tsx:494` | implementer `(message, options?: …)` | **reads** — forwards to `setConfirmState` `:496` |
| `app-shell/.../ActionConfirmDialog.tsx:50,55,58` | terminal reader | **reads** `title`, `cancelText`, `confirmText` |
| `react/.../useActionRunner.ts:26`, `react/.../ActionContext.tsx:35` | re-declares `onConfirm?: ConfirmationHandler` | pass-through |
| `components/.../page-header-action-i18n.test.tsx:83` | test double | no |

**Counter-probe A (method sensitivity).** Same grep applied to `ToastHandler` — a sibling
whose options bag is known-live — finds its two-argument producers at
`ActionRunner.ts:1136` and `:1151`. The method detects two-argument calls; the
non-zero result above is not a search artifact.

**Counter-probe B (positive control on the same lines).** `message` — indisputably live —
travels through *identical syntax at the identical call sites*:
`setConfirmState({ open: true, message, options, resolve })` at `:192` and `:496`,
rendered at `ActionConfirmDialog.tsx:51` (`message`) beside `:50/:55/:58` (`options`).
There is no methodological asymmetry that could make `message` real and `options`
spurious — they are read by the same component from the same state object.

## Reverse-verification (ablation)

Narrowed the type to `(message: string) =` `Promise< boolean >` in
`packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`, rebuilt `@object-ui/core`, type-checked.

**⚠️ First ablation run was a FALSE GREEN.** I edited `src` only and got 0 errors. Before
reading that as a result I checked whether the mutation had reached the consumer:
`packages/core/dist/actions/ActionRunner.d.ts:393` still carried the two-parameter form.
`app-shell` resolves `@object-ui/core` through `dist/index.d.ts` →
`dist/actions/index.d.ts:8` → `ActionRunner.js`, so the un-rebuilt leg measured the
*unmutated* tree. Rebuilding `core` and proving the narrowed form present at
`dist/actions/ActionRunner.d.ts:393` produced the real result.

Predictions were recorded **before** the run:

| # | Predicted | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `ObjectView.tsx` TS2554 "Expected 1 arguments, but got 2" | ✅ `ObjectView.tsx(1399,13): error TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 2.` |
| 2 | `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:190` fails — 2 required params vs 1-param target | ✅ `TS2345` + `TS7006` ×2 (richer than predicted) |
| 3 | `RecordDetailView.tsx:494` **no error** (its `options?:` is optional) | ✅ absent from output |
| 4 | `packages/core` stays clean | ✅ 0 errors, exit 0 |

Baseline (closure built, unmutated): **0 errors, exit 0**.
Ablated: **4 errors, exit 2** — all in `packages/app-shell`, none in `packages/core`.

```
src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx(190,59): error TS2345: Argument of type '(message: any, options: any) =' Promise< boolean > 'is not assignable to parameter of type' ConfirmationHandler'.
src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx(190,60): error TS7006: Parameter 'message' implicitly has an 'any' type.
src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx(190,69): error TS7006: Parameter 'options' implicitly has an 'any' type.
src/views/ObjectView.tsx(1399,13): error TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 2.
```

Restored: source reverted, **`core` rebuilt on the restore leg too**, narrowed form proven
**absent** from `dist`, `app-shell` type-check back to **0 errors / exit 0**,
`git status --porcelain` empty, `git diff origin/main...HEAD` empty.

## The published-surface question the dispatch asked me to answer

The dispatch asked whether *"an implementer who wrote `(msg, opts) =` … still type-checks
against a one-parameter type"* makes removal safe. **Measured answer: no — the premise is
half-true, and the half that is false is the common case.**

- **Bare form `(message, options) =` …** (contextually typed, both params *required*):
  **rejected.** A source signature may not have more *required* parameters than its
  target. Observed as `TS2345` plus two `TS7006` implicit-any errors under
  `noImplicitAny`. This is the natural way to write it, and it is what this repo's own
  `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:190` does.
- **Explicitly-optional form `(message: string, options?: { … }) =` …**: **accepted** —
  optional params do not count toward required arity. `RecordDetailView.tsx:494` survives.

So the escape hatch exists but is not the default; an external implementer who wrote the
obvious two-parameter handler gets a compile break. `@object-ui/core` is public
(`private` unset, `v17.6.0`, `files: ["dist", …]`) and the type is reachable from the
package entry through the re-export chain above — so this is a genuine narrowing of a
published `.d.ts`.

**Precedent in this exact file**: `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:82-87` documents
objectui#4040, where a *one-parameter declaration was a narrower restatement* of a
two-parameter implementation and nothing caught it. Removing `options` would reintroduce
that same shape deliberately.

## Why I stopped

Three independent stop conditions from the dispatch all fired:

1. **Premise falsified** (回翻条款) — a live producer exists; stop at zero commits.
2. **"If any consumer reads `options` … STOP and report"** — three do, and one is a
   terminal render of localized strings.
3. **File-surface breach** — my declared surface is
   `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` + its tests. Every compile break lands in
   `packages/app-shell` (4 errors, 2 files) and the feature repair would be a third file.
   `packages/core` alone stays green, which is exactly why a runner-scoped search read
   this as a clean removal.

I did not add a pin test or a "keep and document" comment either — choosing that
resolution would itself be re-ruling the card, which the 回翻条款 forbids.

## For the maintainer

The card's option 2 ("a producer returns") is not a future condition — **a producer never
left**. Suggested re-triage:

- **Recommended — close as not-a-defect / re-scope to documentation.** `options` is live,
  localized and user-reachable. The correct minimal follow-up, if any, is a comment at
  `ActionRunner.ts:462` naming the out-of-runner producer so the next liveness sweep does
  not re-derive "no producers" from the runner alone.
- **Not recommended — remove.** Breaks a shipped admin feature's localization, breaks
  `app-shell`'s compile, and narrows a published `.d.ts` against implementers who wrote
  the natural two-parameter form.

Two secondary observations, recorded rather than filed (both are facets of this card's own
subject, and filing them while the card is in decision would just be noise):

1. `RecordDetailView.tsx:494`'s handler is fed **only** by the runner, so *its* `options`
   is in fact always `undefined` — the parameter is live on the `ObjectView` path and
   inert on the `RecordDetailView` path. The card's "dead-in-practice" reading is correct
   for exactly one of the two implementations.
2. `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:190` and `RecordDetailView.tsx:494` are near-duplicate
   confirm-runtime implementations feeding the same `ActionConfirmDialog`.

Branch `claude/issue-5205-confirmation-handler-options` was pushed as an empty write-route
probe and carries **zero commits**; no PR opened.

## 回翻条款 — premise falsified. Moving to `needs-user-decision`.

PM round 21, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`. ⛔ Not a ruling — reporting the fork. Zero commits; nothing was changed.

**`options` is not declared-but-never-produced.** It is produced **outside ActionRunner**: `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:1397` calls `confirmHandler(message, {title, confirmText, cancelText})` with all three fields localized through `t()`, and `ActionConfirmDialog.tsx:50/55/58` renders them. The handler is typed `ConfirmationHandler` at `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:78`, so the published type is invoked with a populated bag. It is reachable UI, not dead code — `handleDeleteView` is wired at `ObjectView.tsx:2472` (`onDeleteView={isAdmin ? handleDeleteView : undefined}`) and `:2486`.

**Nothing regressed.** `git blame` dates the call and its three i18n keys to 2026-08-10 (`5bfaabde0`, `36ae2705b4`) — **before** the #4314 ruling (2026-08-17) and before the triage (2026-08-19). The card's and the grading's shared error was scope: **the search was runner-scoped**, and the producer is one package over. Worth keeping as a method note — "no producer" is only as wide as where you looked.

**Removing it would delete a working feature, not inert surface**: the delete-view dialog loses its title and both button labels, falling back to generic `actionConfirm.*` strings; app-shell fails to compile in two files outside the declared surface; and a published `.d.ts` narrows.

### The published-surface question I put to the dev, answered

My dispatch asked whether TypeScript's tolerance of extra parameters makes the removal safe. **Half-true, and the false half is the common case**: a bare `(msg, opts) => …` is **rejected** — two *required* parameters cannot satisfy a one-parameter target — while only the explicitly-optional `(msg, opts?: {…})` form survives. So removal is a genuine breaking narrowing for the natural spelling.

In-file precedent the dev found: `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:82-87` carries a comment about objectui#4040, where a one-parameter declaration was a narrower restatement of a two-parameter implementation and nothing caught it. Removing `options` would deliberately reintroduce that shape.

### Method note worth keeping — a false green, caught

The dev's first ablation leg edited `src` only and produced **0 errors**. Rather than reading that as a result, it checked reachability and found `packages/core/dist/actions/ActionRunner.d.ts:393` still carrying the two-parameter form: app-shell resolves `@object-ui/core` through `dist`, so the un-rebuilt leg had measured the **unmutated** tree. It rebuilt, proved the narrowed form present in `dist`, and only then re-ran — 4 errors, all in app-shell, none in `packages/core`. **That distribution is exactly why a runner-scoped search reads this as a clean removal.**

### The fork

The card's two options no longer partition the space: its option 2 ("a producer returns") is not a future condition — a producer never left.

- **A (dev's recommendation)** — keep the parameter, and add a comment at `ActionRunner.ts:462` naming the out-of-runner producer so the next liveness sweep does not re-derive "no producers" from the runner alone.
- **B** — remove it anyway: needs a new dispatch covering `packages/app-shell`, replacement for three localized strings, and a breaking-change changeset. Deletes working localization for no measured benefit.
- **C** — split: `RecordDetailView.tsx:494`'s handler **is** fed only by the runner, so *its* `options` really is always undefined. That half is genuinely inert.

⛔ I am not choosing. Returning unassigned.

Two things the dev deliberately did **not** file, recording them here instead because both are facets of this card while it is in decision: the `RecordDetailView.tsx:494` inert half above, and the fact that `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:190` and `RecordDetailView.tsx:494` are near-duplicate confirm runtimes feeding one dialog — a deduplication candidate whose right shape depends on how you rule here.

## Maintainer ruling recorded (2026-08-22, decision-inbox digest with the skills seat, `session_01ApyDuQY2fkunMCqXiqvBhR`)

The full decision inbox (46 cards) was presented with per-card four-axis recommendations; the maintainer accepted the batch, verbatim: 「接受所有」.

**Ruled:** Option A — keep the `options` parameter, with an explanatory comment. The parameter is not declared-but-never-produced: a live, localized producer exists outside the runner (`ObjectView.tsx:1397`, the admin delete-view confirmation), so removal would delete a working feature and narrow a published `.d.ts` against the natural two-parameter handler spelling. The deliverable is the comment at `ActionRunner.ts:462` naming the out-of-runner producer, so the next liveness sweep does not re-derive "no producers" from a runner-scoped search alone. Option B (remove anyway) is rejected.

State: `needs-user-decision` removed → `pm:queue` (ready for dispatch).
